    If it's heavier than a breakup

    This app is a self-help tool — not therapy and not medical or mental-health advice. If you're in crisis or thinking about harming yourself, call or text 988 (US Suicide & Crisis Lifeline, 24/7) or text HOME to 741741 (Crisis Text Line). Outside the US, find a local line at findahelpline.org.

    Week 1 · Stop the bleeding

    Cut every easy path back to them. Willpower loses to access, so remove the access.

    1. Wilt Week 1 · Shock & urge

      Everything droops. The urge to reach out is loudest here — so Week 1 removes access instead of relying on willpower.

    2. Root Week 2 · Waves

      Nothing shows above ground yet, but sleep, food and one honest routine are roots going down. The waves still come — they just pass faster.

    3. Bud Week 3 · Rebuilding

      Energy returns in small, closed buds — a plan with friends, a place with no memories. Don't force it open; just keep showing up.

    4. Bloom Week 4 · Your life again

      The flower is not “over it” theatre. It is proof the cracked ground was never the whole story — and Day 31 is yours to design.

    Why 30 days

    Not magic — momentum. Thirty days is long enough for the nightly urge to lose its grip and for new routines to take the slot the relationship used to fill. Your plan was shaped by your intake.

      Stuff-return script

      One message. Logistics only.

      Hi — I have a few of your things (hoodie, book, charger). I can leave them with [friend/building desk] on [day] at [time], or post them. Please do the same with mine. I'd rather keep this to logistics only. Thanks.

      If even this feels like too much contact, a friend can send it. Asking for help here is allowed.

      What you're looking at

      An interactive prototype of “Don't Text Your Ex” — the winning idea from the hackathon niche research: a 30-day no-contact coach whose hero feature is the SOS draft checker. Try the flow: personalize the plan on Today, paste a 2am draft into SOS, save the unsent letter to the Vault, and work the breakup-admin list. The app itself runs in this page only and resets on reload — the feedback comments at the bottom are the one live part, stored so every visitor can read them.

      The design follows the Appllama app-design rules: one locked accent color, semantic light/dark palettes, a fixed shape scale (pill actions, 16px cards, 12px inputs), native-style tab bar and bottom sheets, tabular numerals for counters, and motion kept under 300 ms with Reduce Motion respected.

      The artwork carries meaning, not decoration: on Today, chat bubbles dissolve behind a person walking toward sunrise (letting go); in SOS, an urge-wave diagram shows the peak at ~45 seconds and the fade by 90; in Plan, a plant moves from wilted in cracked earth to bloom across the four phases — Wilt, Root, Bud, Bloom; and in the Vault, a heart mended with gold kintsugi seams stands for “mended, not erased.”

      The numbers behind it (from the research, 2026-11-11)

      • Price: $29 one-time; founding offer $19 for the first 50 buyers. Free tier: 1 free SOS check. Sold via a merchant of record (Paddle: 5% + $0.50 per sale) because Stripe is invite-only preview in Indonesia.
      • What people pay today: Mendaly Premium $7.99/mo or $49.99/yr (mendaly.com); Haven Pro $59.99/yr or $12.99/mo is planned pricing, listed as “coming soon” (haven.loriccoandco.com); couples therapy $100–$300 per session (ourritual.com).
      • Why it's a one-player product: the customer is 18–35, in the first 0–14 days after a breakup, phone in hand late at night — no partner needs to join, no bank linking, no app-store review (web-first).
      • Honest caveats: the breakup-coach space is crowded at the generic level; the research rates confidence “moderate-high” that this is the best of the niches evaluated, “moderate” that it wins the hackathon. Breakup search demand is season-free (“how to get over a breakup” search index ranges only 87–112 across the year, per movingonwell.com).
